**On-call handoff — gateway 503s**

**Root cause:** `dep-4471` (a.novak, "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation", deployed 02:12–02:14) flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest` from `false` to `true`. That change stopped connections from being reused per request, so the pool (fixed size 20) filled up and stayed full. Every error in the log is the same: `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting N)`, with the wait queue climbing past 70 by the end of the log.

**Impact window:** started 2026-03-14 02:14:18 UTC, about 30 seconds after the deploy finished. Still ongoing as of the last log line, 03:59:27 UTC — no recovery seen in the data. Affected routes: `/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/checkout`, spread across all four backend services (billing, orders, catalog, accounts). `/health` kept returning 200 the whole time, so the gateway process itself never went down — it just ran out of connections.

**Scope:** gateway only. `worker.log` for the same window shows no errors and low db wait times, so background jobs were unaffected — they run on a separate pool.

**Roll back:** `dep-4471` on the gateway service. Revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false` (it should go back with the rest of that deploy's config, generation 119).
